Methods specify purified six-His ASKA PfkA/FbaA, substrates and enzyme concentrations, ATP, potassium MOPS and the one-hour assay.
The primary methods specify the ASKA tagged preparations and conditions for the combined PfkA/FbaA assay.
PfkA with S7P and ATP produces candidate SBP; FbaA-only and no-enzyme controls do not. SBP was quantified with F1,6BP calibration because no authentic standard was available.
The primary combined-enzyme assay identifies the two-step route. Results use m/z369.0 while Methods use367.0; the internal discrepancy remains explicit.
Adding FbaA to PfkA/S7P/ATP yields measured E4P and DHAP; PfkA alone yields candidate SBP without those products. The five separate controls constrain the interpretation.
The primary methods identify E. coli PfkA cloning, pET-28b expression, His-affinity preparation and coupled kinase conditions; S7P is supplied as its Ba salt.
The E. coli PfkA S7P comparison reports apparent Km2.5 mM and kcat0.25 s−1, versus F6P0.065 mM and1.2 s−1; the S7P catalytic-efficiency entry is retained as reported, not recalculated.
The issuing reference protein annotation places PfkA in the cytoplasm, retaining the annotation evidence role rather than claiming a new experiment.
The exact cytosol GO annotation supplies IDA evidence and its cited localization studies. Location is not inferred from the protein SUBUNIT field.
The reviewed reference annotation supports Mg2+ dependence, separate from ATP as a consumed core cosubstrate. The 2020 assay includes Mg but does not titrate an S7P-specific requirement.
The issuing annotation gives catalytic and structural Zn sites, two Zn per subunit. Site capacity is not equal to solution occupancy in every purified preparation.
The older abstract reports two Zn per enzyme dimer; this is retained as a preparation/source discrepancy, not silently changed to the newer per-subunit capacity.
The native annotation reports active Co2+ metalloprotein alternatives to Zn. This is older biochemical annotation, not a claim that adding this ion stimulates every holoenzyme preparation.

The native annotation reports active Mn2+ metalloprotein alternatives to Zn. This is older biochemical annotation, not a claim that adding this ion stimulates every holoenzyme preparation.

Methods distinguish untagged pLEM1 purification from His-tagged pLEM5 WT/mutants, and specify the aerobic Tris-buffer challenge assay.

The primary Results/Discussion describe Ni2+ with this sign under the purified canonical FbaA assay. Time- and concentration-dependent inhibition; Zn-site substitution is supported, not direct SBP kinetics.

The primary Results/Discussion describe Cu2+ with this sign under the purified canonical FbaA assay. Substantial inhibition in vitro; the authors caution that cytoplasmic copper is mainly cuprous, so physiological Cu2+ regulation is not established.

The primary Results/Discussion describe low added Zn2+ with this sign under the purified canonical FbaA assay. Slight activation at low added Zn; full loading requires the separate denaturation/metallation treatment.

The primary Results/Discussion describe higher added Zn2+ with this sign under the purified canonical FbaA assay. Very slight inhibition at higher added Zn; this does not negate the essential catalytic Zn role.

The primary Results/Discussion describe Co2+ with this sign under the purified canonical FbaA assay. Slight stimulation under this preparation/assay; alternative Co metalloprotein annotations are separate evidence.
Purification of untagged pLEM1 FbaA was confirmed by sensitivity to100 µM EDTA; this is an independent preparation-specific chelator effect.
Figure7A uses as-purified FbaA20 nM and Ni16 µM with His100 µM or reduced glutathione1 mM; the untagged purification is described separately.
Histidine protects Ni-challenged FbaA: about20% activity loss versus70% without histidine. The positive sign is conditional protection against Ni, not direct activation of untreated FbaA.
Reduced glutathione enhances Ni-dependent FbaA inhibition. The rcnA/gshA comparison supports a cellular contribution; the proposed delivery mechanism is not uniquely established.

The primary abstract specifies six-His FruR, asymmetric consensus/operator binding, tetramer context and negative pfkA regulation.
The native mode is negative for Cra regulation of the pfkA promoter. This and REG0-4838 represent the same BS785 biological-site context rather than two independent mechanisms.
The exact transcription unit joins promoter PM0-46536, binding site BS785 and pfkA gene EG10699.
The source specifically identifies pfkA as negatively regulated by FruR after consensus/operator binding experiments.
The issuing Gene record grounds the pfkA expression endpoint, b3916 in MG1655; BW25113 or historical assay preparations remain separate.
Native Cra regulation of the epd promoter is negative. Its effect on fbaA is carried through the epd-pgk-fbaA transcriptional unit, not a demonstrated separate fbaA operator.
The native epd promoter transcription unit includes EG10282 (fbaA), EG10703 (pgk) and EG10368 (epd). Shared promoter entries are not distinct regulatory mechanisms.
The issuing Gene record grounds fbaA/b2925 as the expression endpoint; it does not establish direct binding at an isolated fbaA promoter.
The abstract identifies thermal-shift/MST and EMSA assays on Cra, with F1P and FBP comparisons; full construct methods were not acquired.

F1P impairs Cra DNA-binding affinity, while FBP neither binds Cra nor impairs its operator binding in the reported tests. The paper also studies a distinct Bacillus CggR protein whose FBP response is not transferred to Cra.
The independent native generic D-fructofuranose1P class links CHEBI58674. The separate FRU1P beta species belongs only to the source-defined ligand complex.
The native epd promoter regulation has positive mode for cAMP-CRP; the fbaA endpoint is linked by the operon, not a distinct bound fbaA promoter.
The epd-pgk-fbaA transcription unit provides the source path to fbaA.
In glucose, deleting the CRP-cAMP site had little effect, whereas crp or cya loss strongly reduced gapB/epd P0 activity. The authors infer an indirect CRP-cAMP effect under these conditions.
The exact issuing fbaA record grounds the downstream operon expression endpoint.
Glucose stimulation of gapB/epd P0 depends on ptsG-encoded EIIGlc. This is expression-system evidence, not a purified direct DNA-binding or enzyme-activation assay.
The source transcription unit links the epd promoter to fbaA, preserving the indirect operon context.

The native comment explicitly identifies the csrA51 hypomorphic allele and M9 glucose context.

CsrA attenuation disrupts upper glycolysis; restoring PfkA activity suppresses glucose-phosphate stress and increases growth. This supports a positive expression contribution, not a new physical RNA-binding claim.
The source states that pfkA expression is reduced in csrA51 and that PfkA overexpression partially rescues its growth defect.
